title: Count Distinct Integers After Removing Zeros
summary: Given a positive integer n, for each integer x from 1 to n, remove all zeros from its decimal representation.
statement: Given a positive integer n, for each integer x from 1 to n, remove all zeros from its decimal representation. Count and return the number of unique integers formed.
constraints: For every x from one through n, delete all zero digits from its decimal representation.
Return the number of distinct resulting positive integers.
hints: Every result is a zero-free integer no greater than n, and every such integer occurs by choosing x equal to itself.
Count positive integers at most n whose decimal digits contain no zero.
A tight digit DP tracks position, whether the number has started, and whether the prefix equals n.
The bijection reduces the original many-to-one deletion process to this exact zero-free count.
editorial: The bijection reduces the original many-to-one deletion process to this exact zero-free count.
